summary: Proverbs sends the sluggard to watch an ant at work. Ants are small and lack strength, yet they gather their food while it is available in summer.

senses.definition: A small insect that gathers food. Its habit of preparing ahead supplies a lesson in wisdom.

evidence.note: The singular directs the lazy person to observe the ant. Verses 7–8 describe it storing food at harvest without an overseer.
The plural names the first of four small, wise creatures. The ants prepare food in summer.

note: Payne Smith includes both the insect and its nest under the Syriac form; the comparative study questions the insect sense. Kogan also questions whether Akkadian namlu is native. The cross-reference תַּגְמוּל is already treated under gamal in Ps 116:12.
